text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

RZECZPOSPOLITA - Leszek Balcerowicz, the leader of the centrist Union for Freedom (UW), has decided to run for parliament in the heavily populated and industrialised Katowice province. During his campaign Balcerowicz will present a mining sector modernisation programme for the region.
- Poland's music record sales soared in March with the three most successful albums selling a total of 160,000 copies, a report by ZPAV audio and video producers association said.
- General Motors (GM) Poland is planning to start assembly of Opel Corsa passenger cars at the Zeran assembly line in Warsaw, the company's president Scott Mackie said.

- The national air carrier LOT Polish Airlines will slash fare prices on round-trip routes from Warsaw to New York to $669, from Warsaw to Chicago to $759 and on the Warsaw-Miami route to $829 from April 10 to June 14 this year, LOT said.
- The first tourist and intercity buses will roll off the Volvo Bus Poland assembly line in Wroclaw southeastern Poland in autumn this year, Volvo said.

- A subsidiary of Allish Irish Banks has bought a 9.4 percent stake in listed Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) worth 18.9 million pounds from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), AIB foreign investment director David McCrossan said.

- Japan's Isuzu motoring firm will start construction of its planned diesel engine plant in the Tychy area of the Katowice Special Economic Zone in May this year, Isuzu's European production project manager Hisaomi Sasaki said.

- The policy of appreciation of the zloty by the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, in the years 1994-1996 favoured imports at the cost of exports, leading to a $12.59 billion current account deficit which threatens the country's economic security, Polish Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said.

- The Polish branch of the international Novartis pharmaceutical concern, in operation as of this year after the merger of Ciba and Sandoz, will report sales worth 650 million zlotys by the end of 1997, Novartis Poland president Tapani Sura said.
- The Warsaw Centrum municipality and the listed Elektrim industrial and trading conglomerate will form the Trasa Swietokrzyska joint venture to construct a new bridge on the Vistula river in Warsaw.
In return for financing the scheme Elektrim will receive the Port Praski river port, the municipality said.
